title: Cutmap prioritization heatmap — Sprint 25 console surface plan
content:
Purpose: quick, defensible cutlist + heatmap to finalize Sprint 25 scope for console rollouts and lightweight tooling. This doc captures the triage decisions from the July 6 grooming session, rationale for cuts, and follow-ups for design/engineering pairing. Use this as the authoritative cutlist to sync with SRE and Solutions Eng before code freeze.

Context and constraints:
- Sprint window: Jul 13 — Jul 26 (2 weeks). Team capacity limited due to 2 engineers on on-call rotation and one holiday.
- Must preserve: canary rollout surface, basic tracing hooks, and rollback policy UI. These are customer SLO blockers for Dedicated onboarding.
- Nice-to-have items can move to sprint backlog if we hit early shippable milestones. Prioritization is risk + customer-impact weighted.

Heatmap methodology (quick):
- X axis = implementation cost (est. dev + infra effort: low/med/high).
- Y axis = customer impact (production reliability, migration friction, revenue enablement).
- Color = shipping risk (green low, amber med, red high).
- Tickets assessed by product + design + one tech lead. T-shirt sizing used for speed (S, M, L).

Triage summary (top-level decisions):
1) Mandatory for Sprint 25 (must ship):
   - RI-4235 Add per-route token & latency breakdown to route details (S, green) — required for CS churn reduction. Keep.
   - RI-4260 Canary traffic percent slider + suggested defaults (M, amber) — keep minimal UI with defaults, postpone advanced scheduling.
   - RI-4281 Rollback action + audit event linkage (S, green) — keep.
2) Deferred to Sprint 26 (cut):
   - RI-4312 Visual diffs for model rollout compares (L, red) — valuable but large surface; defer.
   - RI-4299 Multi-tenant routing editor UX polish (M, red) — postpone until Dedicated capacity metrics land.
   - RI-4307 Inline explainability snippets in the console (M, red) — move to backlog for post-launch.
3) Move to stretch/if-time:
   - RI-4273 Autosuggest for route names based on infra tags (S, green) — low cost, keep as stretch.
   - RI-4251 Lightweight template for common canary configs (S, green) — keep as stretch.

Rationale notes per major ticket:
- RI-4235: Customer success flagged this as the #1 blocker for onboarding existing Dedicated pilot. Implementation plan: add new section under Route > Metrics that fetches precomputed token buckets (backend already exposes endpoint). Design will reuse existing metric panel components. Acceptance criteria: token and latency rows present; export CSV; unit tests for CSV endpoint.

- RI-4260: UX decision to ship a single slider + three recommended presets (Low / Default / Aggressive). Avoid complex cron-based scheduling for Sprint 25. Engineering to implement server-side validation to prevent >100% traffic routing. Acceptance: slider persists per-route, preview shows estimated success rate.

- RI-4281: Rollback action needs audit log link and a guard (two-step confirm). Use existing audit API; implementation should not add new DB tables. Acceptance: rollback triggers existing operation id, audit link surfaces in toast.

Open questions & risks (notes to triage):
- Migration risk for customers with custom rollout scripts: do we provide an export/import compatibility path? Action: Solutions Eng to surface top 5 accounts and escalate if needed (owner: Luca).
- Data retention and cost for per-route token history: backend has 90-day retention; Product to confirm this is acceptable for sales demos.
- Cross-team dependency: RI-4312 (visual diffs) depends on research branch that isn't scheduled this quarter. If that completes earlier, we can reprioritize.

Design notes / wireframe pointers (quick):
- Route details page: add a small accordion titled "Traffic & Cost" containing token/latency rows. Small inline tooltip explaining token units. (Design: Samira to attach quick mock in confluence link).
- Canary slider: 280px horizontal slider, preset buttons below, compact mobile fallback. Keep interactions keyboard accessible.
- Rollback: modal with reason dropdown + optional freeform text, copy of last deployment metadata.

Acceptance criteria checklist (for each must-ship ticket):
- Frontend: passes accessibility quick audit (contrast + keyboard focus).
- Backend: existing endpoints reused where possible; no new heavy aggregations.
- E2E: basic happy-path scenario covered in Cypress test (happy + one failure scenario).
- Docs: one-page "what changed" in console release notes and update to onboarding playbook.

Implementation plan & owners (rough):
- Week 1: Devs pair on RI-4235 + RI-4281 (Evan owner, Samira design). Backend tweaks and small UI panel.
- Week 2: Finish slider and presets (Dev: Priya), QA and staging verification, docs.
- Buffer: reserve 20% sprint time for on-call interruptions.

Follow-ups & action items:
- Design: Samira to post high-fidelity mocks by Jul 9 (link in Confluence).
- Engineering: Evan to create subtask breakdown in Jira and add estimates by Jul 10.
- Solutions Eng: Luca to produce account impact matrix for top 5 Dedicated pilots by Jul 11.
- PM: Maya will draft release notes and coordinate with growth for messaging.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the canary UX conservative: customers like predictable defaults. Resist feature-creep (visual diffs are tempting but big).
- Remember to flag cost metrics to Finance if per-route history increases storage beyond expectations.

Appendix: quick ticket list with short status tags (for sprint board):
- RI-4235 (must) — frontend ready + backend endpoint available
- RI-4260 (must) — design mock in progress
- RI-4281 (must) — backend hooks available
- RI-4273 (stretch) — research spike approved
- RI-4251 (stretch) — template copy ready for i18n pass
- RI-4312 (defer) — research branch pending

If anything changes before Jul 10 grooming follow-up, ping #console-product and update this doc.

Links referenced: RI-4235, RI-4260, RI-4281, RI-4312, Confluence: /console/rollouts/heatmap-gtm, PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/982
